title: Ordinary curve points characterized by delta and branch number
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $X$ a reduced finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-pure-dimension], and $x\in X(k)$ a closed point. Let $
u:\widetilde X	o X$ be the disjoint union of the normalizations of its reduced irreducible components [def-sc-normalization]. Put $b=|
u^{-1}(x)|$ and $\delta=\dim_k((
u_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde X})_x/\mathcal O_{X,x})$, using sheaf direct image on opens and the natural inclusion of local rings. These numbers are finite, $b\ge1$, and $\delta\ge b-1$. Equality holds if and only if the maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to
$$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong k[[t_1,\ldots,t_b]]/(t_it_j\mid i
e j),$$
with formal power series as in [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. This condition is called an ordinary $b$-fold point. An ordinary one-fold point is exactly a smooth point [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; an ordinary two-fold point is exactly an ordinary node. Thus smooth points have $\delta=0$, and nodes have $b=2$ and $\delta=1$.

source.place: Appendix B, ordinary n-fold points and the inequality/equality characterization preceding Lemma B.1, printed pp. 56--57. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $B=(\nu_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde X})_x$, $H=\widehat A$ and $C=\varprojlim_n B/\mathfrak m_A^nB$. The local comparison gives $1\le b<\infty$, $\delta<\infty$, $\delta=\dim_k(C/H)$, and $C=\overline H$. Here $H$ is reduced Noetherian local with structural residue field $k$, and $C=B\otimes_A H$ is finite over $H$; also $B=A$ at smooth points.

source.place: Tags 0C1U (equation-multicross), 0C1V (lemma-multicross-algebra); normalization and completion: varieties.tex Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant).

proof.text: The branch coordinates identify $C$ with $D=\prod_{i=1}^b k[[t_i]]$ and the residue image of $H$ with $\Delta k\subset k^b$. Set $P=\rho^{-1}(\Delta k)$ for the constant-coefficient map $\rho:D\to k^b$. Then $H\subset P$, and $D/H\to k^b/\Delta k$ is surjective with kernel $P/H$. Since $\dim_k(k^b/\Delta k)=b-1$, dimension additivity gives $\delta\ge b-1$, with equality exactly when $H=P$.

source.place: Tags 0C1U (equation-multicross), 0C1V (lemma-multicross-algebra); normalization and completion: varieties.tex Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant).

proof.text: The axes calculation gives $P\cong R_b=k[[T_1,\ldots,T_b]]/(T_iT_j:i\ne j)$, so equality implies the required $k$-algebra presentation. For the converse apply normalization-pair invariance to $H\cong R_b\cong P$. Its hypotheses hold: Step 1 gives reduced Noetherian local $H$ with structural residue field $k$, finite normalization $C$, and finite-dimensional $C/H$; Step 2 gives its $b$ nonzero local-domain factors. The axes calculation supplies these properties for $P$ and its normalization $D$. Invariance therefore identifies $C/H$ with $D/P$ as $k$-vector spaces, giving $\delta=b-1$.

source.place: Tags 0C1U (equation-multicross), 0C1V (lemma-multicross-algebra); normalization and completion: varieties.tex Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant).

proof.text: If $x$ is smooth, $B=A$ gives $\delta=0$, hence $b=1$ and the equality criterion makes $x$ ordinary one-fold. Conversely $H\cong k[[T]]$ at an ordinary one-fold point. This power-series ring is regular; completion regularity descends to $A$, and the separable-residue smoothness criterion on an affine finite-type chart makes $x$ smooth. The residue extension is $k/k$.

source.place: Tags 0C1U (equation-multicross), 0C1V (lemma-multicross-algebra); normalization and completion: varieties.tex Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant).

proof.text: The nodal criterion over algebraically closed $k$ says that a node has a ring isomorphism $H\cong R_2$. Step 1 gives the finite normalization and finite defect; Step 2 identifies its local-domain factors with the actual fibre points. Thus the axes calculation and normalization-pair invariance apply and give $b=2$ and $\delta=1$, even when this ring isomorphism is not $k$-linear. The equality criterion then supplies the $k$-algebra isomorphism, so the point is ordinary two-fold. Conversely an ordinary two-fold point has a ring isomorphism $H\cong R_2$, hence is a node; the same invariance gives $b=2$ and $\delta=1$.

source.place: Tags 0C1U (equation-multicross), 0C1V (lemma-multicross-algebra); normalization and completion: varieties.tex Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant).

mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q97-9e020374c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no fixes. I read the item in full, all four new nodes, and every cited statement (nodal-point local criterion, the three pbc regularity/smoothness nodes, and the five same-tag nodes in the report).

This is the fourth head of this re-split. eb8e750c088, 380b294f0531 and f0ef96862eaa were all PASSed and then refused at landing ('not in the live DAG'). In clones/live and clones/side-live the item is still the 11-step 'split' node, and the batch-5 re-split note is released.

What changed since f0ef: the four new nodes are byte-identical (same sha256). The item's statement, stmt_deps, source and Lean fields are unchanged. The only change is in Step 5: it now invokes Step 1 (finite normalization and finite defect) and Step 2 (fibre points are the local-domain factors) before applying pair invariance, and adds two matching 'uses'. This is a real improvement in hypothesis checking.

Assembly, step by step:
- Steps 1-2: H is contained in P = rho^-1(Delta k), and D/H maps onto k^b/Delta k with kernel P/H. So delta >= b-1, with equality iff H = P.
- Step 3: the axes node gives R_b iso P, so equality gives the presentation. The converse uses pair invariance, whose hypotheses all hold.
- Step 4: power series k[[T]] is regular, regularity descends from the completion, and the separable-residue smoothness criterion applies with residue extension k/k.
- Step 5: the nodal criterion only gives a ring isomorphism, and invariance needs no k-linearity. It gives b = 2 and delta = 1, then the equality criterion gives the k-algebra presentation.

New nodes, all true:
- Axes node: checked b=1, b=2, sD in P, m_P = ker rho kills D/P, and Q(P) = P[1/s].
- Pair invariance: length equals dim_k because every simple factor is k, and b counts primitive idempotents.
- Local data and branch coordinates: specialisations of Stacks 0C1R, 0C3V, 07N9 and 0C0S to algebraically closed k.

No node restates the parent, the four new nodes are of comparable size, and every old argument is carried by a node. No duplicates: split-node-component-normalization is only the b=2 case with a fixed k-algebra nodal completion, and finite-colength-completion-comparison is a generic input. No SGA source is used. The generic tool_uses in Step 4 are accepted.
